long_biography.plain_text:
Born in London and brought to Canada at seven, Michael Urwin Potter entered the Royal Canadian Navy before studying science and operations research. He joined Quasar Systems in 1972, bought the Ottawa consultancy within three years and redirected it from bespoke government work toward reusable software products. Renamed Cognos, the business expanded internationally and became a public leader in business intelligence under his two decades as chief executive.

After stepping down in 1995, Potter moved from corporate management into private investing through Sussex Capital, backing companies including Kinaxis and retaining control of the investment firm. He also returned to aviation, a longstanding interest rooted in his naval service and pilot training. Through Vintage Wings of Canada, he assembled and restored historic aircraft so they could be flown, displayed and used to introduce younger Canadians to aviation history.
